clips.title: EC2 Auto Scaling Warm Pools | Warm Pools | EC2 Auto Scaling
clips.why: The warm pool's settings in the console: the pool state, its size, and what happens to instances when the group scales in.
look: Stopped is one of the pool states: the VM waits with only its disk.
The pool's minimum size is how many VMs wait ready.
The reuse setting decides whether a VM may go back into the pool.
clips.after: Our pools wait Stopped, two lite and two full, and never take a used VM back, so every run gets a fresh one.

clips.title: Amazon EC2 Spot Instances: Automating 2min Notifications
clips.why: Spot machines can be taken back with a two-minute warning, and a program can react to that warning.
look: What the two-minute notice is and where it comes from.
Reacting automatically instead of losing the work.
Why Spot fits work that can stop and start again.
clips.after: On our Spot VMs a small timer watches for that notice; the harness checkpoints and exits as preempted, and the workflow retries on a fresh VM.

practice.q: Complete the tag that a live run keeps moving forward every five minutes.
practice.hint: The tag whose time says the owner is still there.
practice.why: The sweeper reads it to decide whether a claimed VM still has an owner.

practice.q: Which VMs can a Spot interruption hit in our platform?

options.text: VMs of routines that can retry, such as the CI fixer
options.why: Only the Spot groups have Spot machines, and only retryable routines use them.

options.text: Nova's VMs while they wait for a person
options.why: Nova uses on-demand machines, because it waits on people.
The warm pools are on-demand; the Spot groups have no warm pool.

practice.q: Put the ownership of one VM in order.
items: The VM finishes its setup and waits stopped in the warm pool
A run claims it: it is detached and tagged with the run-id and a lease
The run renews the lease every five minutes while it works
The orchestrator crashes and the lease is no longer renewed
The sweeper sees the lease has passed and terminates the VM
practice.why: The group owns it, then the run through its lease, and the sweeper only when nobody does.

practice.q: Why is the sweeper's role allowed to terminate only machines tagged ai-agents:managed=true?

options.text: So a bug in its rules can never touch a machine outside the sandbox fleet
options.why: The role is the outside wall for the sweeper itself: even a wrong rule cannot reach other machines.

options.text: Because AWS needs a tag to terminate a machine
options.why: AWS needs no tag. The condition is our own limit on the role.
Speed is not the point. It is a limit on what the job can destroy.
